name: How do I know if I need more than a basic site evaluation?

mainEntity.name: How do I know if I need more than a basic site evaluation for my project?
mainEntity.text: How do I know if I need more than a basic site evaluation for my project?

acceptedAnswer.text: A basic site evaluation is enough for straightforward properties with obvious access, flat terrain, and limited permitting complexity. You need a deeper feasibility study when the project depends on assumptions that could easily be wrong: utility availability, grading quantity, slope stability, buildable area, easements, or a narrow budget. In Los Angeles, lots with hillside conditions, dense neighboring development, or uncertain infrastructure often require more than a simple walk-through. A deeper study is justified when the result will influence a land purchase, major design commitment, or a construction budget that leaves little room for surprises. The rule of thumb is simple: if a wrong assumption could materially change the project, the evaluation should be more detailed.
acceptedAnswer.description: You likely need a deeper feasibility study if the lot is sloped, has unclear access, suspected soil issues, utility uncertainty, easements, or a project that depends on tight budget and schedule assumptions. If any one of those factors could change the design or cost materially, a basic review is not enough.
